raw_record.question_text:
A simple harmonic transverse wave propagates along the positive direction of the $x$-axis. The equilibrium position of the wave source is at the origin of the coordinate system. The vibration graph of the wave source within $0 \sim 4s$ is shown in the figure. It is known that the wave propagation speed is $0.5\mathsf{m}/\mathsf{s}$.

1. Determine the wavelength of this transverse wave.
2. Determine the distance traveled by the wave source within 4s.

method.method_draft: Read the source vibration graph as a y-versus-t sinusoid: it starts at y=0 at t=0, reaches +4 cm, crosses y=0 again at t=2 s, reaches -4 cm, and returns to y=0 at t=4 s. Thus one full vibration cycle lasts T=4 s and the amplitude is A=4 cm. Use the text-given propagation speed v=0.5 m/s and the wave relation λ=vT to get λ=2 m. For the source distance in 4 s, note that 4 s is one complete period, during which the source moves from 0 to +A, back through 0 to -A, and back to 0, so total path length is A+A+A+A=4A=16 cm.

推理：波速已知 v=0.5 m/s，由波长公式 λ=vT 得 λ=0.5×4=2 m。4 s 是一个完整周期，波源从平衡位置到 +A，再回到平衡位置，再到 -A，最后回到平衡位置，经过的总路程为 A+A+A+A=4A=4×4 cm=16 cm。

method.method_draft: Model the source motion from the graph as y=A sin(ωt), since the curve passes upward through equilibrium at t=0. Read A=4 cm from the dashed ±4 cm levels. Use the visual zero crossing at t=2 s with opposite slope to identify it as half a cycle, so T=2×2 s=4 s; equivalently ω=2π/T=π/2 rad/s. Then compute frequency f=1/T=0.25 Hz and combine with the text-given wave speed using λ=v/f=0.5/0.25=2 m. For source travel distance, use the sine model over t=0 to 4 s: over one full period the absolute displacement path equals the sum of monotonic changes between successive turning points, |0−4|+|4−0|+|0−(−4)|+|−4−0|=16 cm.
